chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ja'far ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Alawi, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas, from Isma'il ibn Ishaq, all together from Abu Rawh Faraj ibn Qurra, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa who said: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) said: 'As for what follows:
Verily, jihad is a gate from the gates of Paradise that God has opened for His special friends, and has permitted for them as an honor from Him and a blessing He has stored up.

And jihad is the garment of taqwa, and the fortified armor of God, and His firm shield. So whoever abandons it out of aversion to it, God will clothe him with the garment of humiliation, and affliction will engulf him, and he will depart from God's pleasure, and he will be abased by pettiness and degradation, and his heart will be sealed with barriers, and truth will be displaced from him through the wasting of jihad, and he will be subjected to humiliation and denied justice.

Beware! I have called you to fight these people night and day, secretly and openly, and I said to you: "Attack them before they attack you!" For by God, no people have ever been attacked in the interior of their homes without being humiliated. But you were complacent and abandoned one another until raids were launched upon you and your homelands were seized from you. This brother of Ghamid — his cavalry has entered al-Anbar and killed Hassan ibn Hassan al-Bakri and driven your cavalry from its positions.

And it has reached me that a man from them would enter upon a Muslim woman and another woman under protection, and would snatch her anklets, her bracelets, her necklaces, and her earrings, and she could not prevent him except by saying 'innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rāji'ūn' and begging for mercy. Then they departed unharmed — no man of them was wounded nor was any blood shed. So if a Muslim man were to die of grief after this, he would not be blamed for it; rather, in my view he would be worthy of it.

How astonishing, how astonishing! By God, it melts the heart and brings sorrow — this gathering of these people upon their falsehood, and your scattering from your truth. So shame on you and woe to you, for you have become a target to be shot at! They raid you and you do not counter-raid; they fight against you and you do not fight back; God is disobeyed and you are pleased.

So when I command you to march against them in the days of summer heat, you say: 'This is the scorching heat of summer — give us respite until the heat cools off from us.' And when I command you to march against them in winter, you say: 'This is the biting cold of winter — give us respite until the cold departs from us.' All of this is fleeing from the heat and the cold! If you flee from heat and cold, then by God you are even more fleeing from the sword!

Give us respite until the intense summer heat subsides from us. And when I ordered you to march against them in winter, you said: This is the bitter cold; give us respite until the cold passes from us. All of this is fleeing from heat and cold. So when you flee from heat and cold, by God, you are even more fleeing from the sword. O you who resemble men but are not real men, with the minds of children and the intellects of secluded women! I would have wished, by God, that I had never seen you and never known you, an acquaintance that, by God, brought regret.

key_terms.أَشْبَاهَ الرِّجَالِ: Resemblers of men — a rebuke meaning they look like men but lack manly character
key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad — striving/fighting in the way of God; here specifically armed defense of Muslim territory
key_terms.الِاسْتِرْجَاعُ: Saying 'innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rāji'ūn' — the Quranic formula of resignation to God (2:156)
key_terms.ثَوْبَ الذُّلِّ: The garment of humiliation — contrasted with the garment of taqwa
key_terms.حَمَارَّةُ الْقَيْظِ: The peak of summer heat; an expression for the most intense heat of the season
key_terms.صَبَارَّةُ الْقُرِّ: The severity of winter cold; an expression for intense cold
key_terms.لِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى: The garment of taqwa — a Quranic metaphor (7:26); jihad as moral armor

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about jihad and the duty of Muslims to defend their lands?
ai.summary: This khutba (sermon) was delivered by Imam Ali (AS) during his caliphate, addressed to his followers in Kufa who were failing to mobilize for jihad against Muawiya's forces. The Imam begins with a theological framing of jihad as a gate to Paradise, then pivots sharply to rebuke his followers for their passivity while enemies raided Muslim lands and violated women's honor. He concludes with a famous lament about those who call him brave but unknowledgeable in war — a charge he refutes by noting he has fought since before the age of twenty, now past sixty.
